cards.title: DeepMind's AlphaGenome 2 Predicts Variant Effects Across Single Cell Types, Trained on 107M+ Cell Profiles
cards.why_it_matters: A major DeepMind lab release with direct implications for genomics-meets-ML research — the conditional architecture redesign and cross-modality imputation are technically novel and the scale is landmark.
cards.summary: AlphaGenome 2 is a conditional DNA sequence model that takes a million-letter sequence plus a target cell type or state as joint input, predicting molecular outputs one condition at a time rather than in parallel. Trained on over 107 million single-cell profiles across 68 tissues, it identifies nearly twice as many expression-altering variants as its predecessor. Cross-modality imputation lets it predict unmeasured readouts from partial inputs. Available via API for non-commercial use.

cards.title: Pooling-Aware Training Boosts ColBERT-Style Multi-Vector Retrieval from 94.6% to 97.8% NanoBEIR Retention at 4× Compression
cards.why_it_matters: A concrete, reproducible training technique for multi-vector retrieval systems — directly relevant if you work on embedding models, RAG pipelines, or efficient search infrastructure.
cards.summary: Token pooling compresses multi-vector document representations by merging similar token embeddings via Ward hierarchical clustering. Standard training with pool_factor=4 retains 94.6% of unpooled NanoBEIR nDCG@10; pooling-aware training raises that to 97.8% at the same 4× storage reduction. The method teaches the encoder to preserve information through merging, implemented in Sentence Transformers with a short reproducible example.

cards.title: EM-DETR Foundation Model for Medical Lesion Detection Beats Prior SOTA by 1–3% Points Across CXR and Mammography
cards.why_it_matters: Example-based detection with heterogeneous label spaces is a real technical challenge in medical AI; the student-teacher strategy for catastrophic forgetting mitigation is a transferable technique.
cards.summary: The authors extend their EM-DETR example-based detection framework into a multi-domain foundation model for medical lesion detection, using a student-teacher strategy to combine datasets with heterogeneous label spaces and reduce catastrophic forgetting. The model exceeds previous SOTA by 1 percentage point in image-level AUC on four CXR findings, and surpasses single-dataset EM-DETR by 2–3 points in mAP50 on CXRs and mammography.
